defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: It compiles is a claim, and a clean log proves only the bottom rung.
A headless run prints values, but only a person at a screen sees pixels.
A pinned clock and a fixed random seed make a run repeat.
Colour textures get the source color hint, and normal maps stay as data.
A loose tolerance gives false passes, and a tight one gives false fails.
A new test must fail on known-bad code and pass on known-good code.
bookends.command: Quiz me on shader verification terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms claim versus evidence, observed versus inferred, headless mode, bench scene, test fixture, golden image, tolerance, false positive, specification oracle and mutation check. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is about making a game, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike does not fit.
